headline: Use one pay-for-use mechanism: a builtin `ffi` module whose plain-Python twins in tools/rt_cpython are the oracle. It has three stages. `@ffi.extern` calls C in both tiers, binding each function at the `def` with dlopen and dlsym, as ctypes does. `lib/pyobj.py` embeds CPython (libpython 3.12+, stable ABI) in both tiers, with AOT as the reference. `pystachy ext` builds abi3 (3.12+) or abi3t (3.15+) extension modules of `@ffi.export` functions, AOT only. A prototype rebased on current main (4dc548a) passes `make verify` 19/19 and gives byte-identical IR for every program that does not use the FFI. All 15 blocking issues from the last review are fixed. Recommended merge order: S0, S1, S3, S2, as #4 §4 and #108 point to S3.

jit_aot.pystachy_to_c: Both JIT and AOT, from the same IR. `@ffi.extern("lib")` stubs bind when the `def` runs: dlopen(lib, RTLD_NOW|RTLD_LOCAL), plus RTLD_DEEPBIND under the JIT so lli's own libraries cannot shadow it, then dlsym in that handle. The library is neither linked nor passed to lli, so JIT, AOT and the ctypes twin bind the same library. A call costs 3.9 ns (AOT). The one tier difference is `@extern("")`, which sees each process's own libraries; it is documented.
jit_aot.pystachy_to_cpython: Both JIT and AOT, with AOT as the reference tier. lib/pyobj.py is subset code calling CPython's stable ABI through @extern("python") against PYSTACHY_LIBPYTHON (3.12+, GIL or free-threaded): lli -dlopen in the JIT, linked with an rpath in AOT. Embedding results match the twin on 3.12 to 3.15t in both tiers. The JIT residuals are documented: embedded extension modules load with RTLD_DEEPBIND, and `@extern("")` sees lli's process. The same lib/pyobj.py also runs inside an extension module, against the host interpreter.
jit_aot.cpython_to_pystachy: AOT only. `pystachy ext mod.py` builds an abi3 module (PyInit_, 3.12+ GIL builds) or an abi3t module (PyModExport_, PEP 793/803/820, 3.15+ GIL and free-threaded) from byte-identical program IR, with header-free pyext.c glue. CPython imports shared objects, and `pystachy run` is a separate lli process (#108: not a resident compiler service). An in-process JIT would need libLLVM (117-123 MB) or llvmlite (173 MiB installed, LLVM 22), while the .so imports in 0.27-0.45 ms and an exported call costs about 18-22 ns net. The development loop is S5's compile-on-import cache, which is still AOT.

verification_summary:
Fix report, on the final tree (4051925; most checks ran on d89c8b9, which differs only by one line of a test client):
- make reaches the three-stage fixed point (225,035 lines of IR); runtime.py's IR is byte-identical to base's.
- make irsame REF=4dc548a: 1240 programs identical, plus 69 extra files.
- tests/run.sh: 1933/0.
- check_runtime, rtabi (0 mismatches), check-ir (597 programs) and make lint all pass.
- tests/ffi/run.sh: 93/0 on 3.12, 3.13, 3.14, 3.15 and 3.15t; 72/0 on 3.13t and 3.14t (ext skipped by design); 34/0 on 3.11; 91/0 with the CPython-hosted compiler.
- probe5: 215 same, 0 different, with 3 documented deviations.
- refute5 (every case of the 15 stage-4 blocking issues): 64 same, 0 different, with 2 documented deviations.
- UBSan trap mode: 46 same, 0 different.
- make verify: 19/19 in 694 s (ffi step 93/0).

Re-checked today by me:
- The patch applies cleanly to origin/main 4dc548a, which is still main per git ls-remote.
- tests/ffi/run.sh on 3.13: 93/0.
- The new tests against the pre-fix compiler: 54 passed, 39 failed. The fix report recorded 54/37.
- The document's three examples give identical output under twin, JIT and AOT (C and embedding), and from source+twin and the .so (ext). The .so also loads on 3.12, 3.14, 3.15 and 3.15t (abi3t), and 3.14t gets the guard's ImportError.
- Import time, median of 21 processes: 0.27-0.45 ms.
- Two undocumented deviations found: exported functions have no __doc__ or signature, and import from a subinterpreter raises ImportError.

Not run: an independent refutation of the stage-5 fixes, GitHub CI, any platform other than x86-64 Linux/glibc, and distribution builds of 3.15.
open_decisions: Merge order: S1 -> S3 -> S2 (recommended, following #4 §4 and #108), or S1 -> S2 -> S3.
Default --abi for `pystachy ext`: abi3 (recommended) or abi3t; ship both side by side for wheels.
abi3 floor: 3.12 (recommended) or 3.13. Either way 3.11 is excluded, although it has security support until 2027-10.
Free-threaded 3.13t/3.14t: leave the gap, or add a header-free version-specific cp314t build. PEP 779 made 3.14t officially supported.
Embedded stdout: keep exact ordering, which costs about 440 ns on a print right after a pyobj operation, or route all Pystachy output through sys.stdout once CPython is embedded.
Ctrl-C in embedding programs: accept the documented non-finalization, or design a deferred finalization.
str at the extension boundary: byte semantics inside (prototype), or reject non-ASCII by default (typed-ir §7.4 'check or reject'). Issue #120 makes this matter.
pyembed.c uses the deprecated Py_SetProgramName and Py_UTF8Mode. Accept them, or move to PEP 741 PyInitConfig, which is not in the Limited API.
CI: vendor Misc/stable_abi.toml so tools/abi_check.sh runs in verify/CI; make the ffi step fail, not skip, without a shared libpython; run the c_ cases in the python-free stage.
Platforms: x86-64 Linux/glibc only, or also AArch64 Linux and macOS. macOS needs -undefined dynamic_lookup and has no RTLD_DEEPBIND.
Finding libpython: PYSTACHY_LIBPYTHON only, or also a --libpython flag.
caveats: No independent refutation pass ran on the stage-5 fixes (d89c8b9/4051925). The 15 blocking issues were re-checked only by the fixer's refute5.sh, which replays the refuters' cases.

The branch is not split into per-stage PRs. The per-stage line counts in the document (about +165/+50, +50/+60 and +130/+50 in pystachy.py/runtime.c for S1/S2/S3) are attributions of the combined diff, not measured splits.
Tested only on x86-64 Ubuntu 24.04 with glibc and LLVM 18.1.3. 3.13t-3.15t are python-build-standalone builds, and 3.15.0 is two days old.

Remaining documented deviations, not fixed: Ctrl-C in an embedding program does not finalize CPython; release timing of dropped Objects; peak memory about one collector budget (32 MiB) above CPython; @extern("") differs by process; RTLD_DEEPBIND visible under JIT embedding.
Found today and not yet in docs/ffi.md: exported functions lack __doc__ and signature (inspect.signature raises ValueError); import from a subinterpreter raises ImportError.

S1's acceptance item 'run the c_ tests in the python-free stage' is not met. abi_check.sh is not in verify or CI. On a CI runner whose python3 has no shared libpython, the ffi verify step passes while skipping the embedding and extension cases.
The final lint used ruff 0.16.8, not the pinned 0.17.0. The UBSan runtime was installed in the container with apt for make verify.
Per-call cost after the fixes was measured on 3.13 only. The figures for the other versions come from the stage-3 build.
Main may move again: the patch applies to 4dc548a as of 2026-10-11 ~17:45 UTC.
